children: In
Grand Theft Auto VI
, the drug dealers worry about Instagram. As
The Guardian
’s Keza MacDonald put it in her review, “even the narcos are obsessed with their Instagram clout.” In the original
Vice City
, Rockstar gave us the
Scarface

fantasy of a man doing cocaine at a desk large enough to land a helicopter on. In 2026, the same man would have to angle the desk for the light and spend Tuesday afternoon explaining to his associates why they need to post more consistently. The reach has been disappointing.
GTA VI
launched on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, thirteen years after
GTA V

. Rockstar’s day-one figures filed with the SEC put estimated worldwide retail sales through the end of November 19 at US$3.79 billion. Rockstar separately reported 32.5 million copies sold before release. The company also put
GTA V

at nearly 235 million units sold into retail and distribution. That’s the commercial inheritance behind the richest irony of launch week. Rockstar built a Florida where you can steal a car, take it wherever you like, and abandon it in a swamp. Buy the game in a box and once you’ve used the code, the only thing left to lend a friend is the box.
Vice City, now with people in it
The 2002
Vice City

was an ’80s Miami mixtape with a body count. The city now sits inside Leonida, Rockstar’s fictional Florida, alongside the Keys, wetlands, malls, flea markets and whole stretches of road you might follow just to see where they go. Map size is the easiest thing here to oversell. Anyone can make a big map and scatter errands over it until it resembles the home screen of a phone you desperately need to clean out. Rockstar makes it tempting to miss your turn on purpose.
During a demonstration for
The Guardian

, Jason petted a stranger’s dog, took out binoculars to identify a gull, and added it to a wildlife log. There are 62 kinds of birds to spot. Someone at Rockstar understood that the definitive car-theft simulator needed a gull with absolutely no interest in furthering the plot. The music serves a similar purpose. The original score is by Justice, the French duo who made dance music sound like a leather jacket plugged into the mains. The old
Vice City
understood that the right song can make a drive more memorable than the mission at the other end. The new one has enough confidence in its world to let you keep driving.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tJbzMqJGH4k
Rockstar Games’ extended look at GTA VI, captured in-game on PlayStation 5.
Bonnie and Clyde need groceries
GTA V

gave us three men taking turns embodying different strains of American brain damage. This time it’s Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, a couple whose easy score goes bad and who have to decide how much they’re willing to do for each other. There’s a button for holding hands. You can stock the fridge.
The Washington Post

’s Gene Park, testing how the story responded to neglect, wrote, “I even forced Jason to become a total loser”. He had Jason sleep through picking Lucia up from prison and saw different scenes and arguments. Even in a game that can swallow a hundred hours, the guy with the stolen sports car still has to answer a question familiar to anyone who’s ever dated a man with a car. Where the hell were you?
Rockstar’s Rob Nelson told
The Guardian

the team wanted to “provide mechanisms that encourage empathy”. That sounds like what Pixar might put on a slide for investors. Here it shows up in what the game lets you do. Park describes jobs that can end without a shot fired and a night out where introducing your girlfriend to your repellent friends is an actual social problem to solve. Giving you a reason to care what happens after the shooting makes the violence a little less disposable.

Lucia has room to be ruthless, funny, horny and vulnerable, sometimes within the same stretch of the story. MacDonald noticed the difference in the women around her, too, from the rappers trying to make it to the middle-aged drug runner with a beloved purple rifle. There are male strippers. After several decades of debate over the male gaze, Rockstar has worked out that a man can also take his trousers off and disappoint a room full of people.

The increased realism also invites a kind of low-grade domestic misery. Park reports that neglecting food and sleep can hurt a job, and that people notice when you go too long without a shower. MacDonald tried to say hello to a stranger and punched him instead. Some of that friction produces stories you actually want to tell. Some of it sounds like a very expensive way to have a fitness tracker and a parole officer agree about your lifestyle. And the old frat-house writing still turns up in the form of horny pensioners on TV and a golf-club gag about testicles. The sharper the human observation gets, the more those jokes sound like a guy who’s been invited back to the writers’ room because his dad owns the building.
The box is yours. Enjoy the box.
As

, the standard edition costs US$79.99, the Ultimate Edition costs US$99.99, and the boxed standard edition comes with a download code in place of a disc. PC players sat out launch day. The code is the more interesting bit. A disc could circulate among friends or end up on a used-game shelf. A redeemed code leaves you with a handsome piece of shelf decoration. The industry has spent years persuading people that a purchase and an account entitlement are interchangeable. Now it puts the entitlement in a box and lets your childhood do the rest of the marketing.

Downloads are convenient. Nobody particularly misses getting up to switch discs. The point of the box is that it preserves the appearance of a transaction whose terms have changed. Sony and Microsoft can deliver a game to your couch in the middle of the night. Your friend still can’t borrow the one you paid for by picking it up off the coffee table. Apparently the future of retail needed a prop department.
The same pre-order window attracted GTA-themed memecoins and unauthorized sites offering fake early access for crypto. If you remember

children: , you already know how efficiently a recognizable name can move a digital object. What’s funny about the GTA knockoffs is how little of the original business they needed to imitate. A logo, a checkout and the promise of getting in before everyone else will take you surprisingly far. The official business was already good at selling things that cost very little to duplicate. Take-Two reported that recurrent consumer spending, its category for virtual currency, add-ons and similar purchases, accounted for 81% of companywide net revenue in the quarter ended September 30. Rockstar offered a free month of GTA+ with digital pre-orders. Even the satire of hustle culture had a subscription trial at checkout.
Tony Montana would have a discount code

Vice City is American, but its understanding of status travels. In October, Pew Research Center found that one in five American adults regularly got news from TikTok, rising to 39% among adults aged 18 to 29. People all over the West know the experience of opening the same feed for election results, watching somebody accuse the winner of cheating, then discovering the accuser has a discount code for powdered greens. The phone has one set of tools for working out what’s true, becoming famous and shifting inventory. Rockstar’s narcos have grasped that arrangement as well as any lifestyle entrepreneur with a lav mic. Their genuine competitive advantage is that they know they’re criminals.
What makes
VI

interesting is that Rockstar could have simply cashed in on all that recognition. It has instead made a game where a little time spent with another person can matter as much as your next big score. For a weekend at least, it also gave people who live in incompatible feeds something to talk about besides what their feeds had just told them to hate. There’s real pleasure in that, even if the entertainment industry will study the launch and conclude the secret ingredient was a familiar logo and a hundred-dollar edition.

Rockstar has made a place where you can get away with an incredible amount and occasionally choose to be decent. It sold that place to millions of people who used to hand a game to a friend and say, “You have to try this.” Somewhere between the gull, the hand-holding button and the empty box, somebody put a hell of a lot of work into remembering how people behave. Somebody else figured out how to bill both friends.

title: GTA VI Lets You Steal a Car. Try Lending the Game to a Friend.
